ei.title: A Picture Is Worth a Thousand Words
ei.subject: 공통영어2

fullPassage: Paul is a comic writer. He has been drawing many comics about overcoming challenges in communication, and it all began with his experience at the hospital with his mother, Anna. A few years ago, doctors told Anna that she had Parkinson's disease. It is a progressive disease which affects the nervous system. It makes muscles shake and gradually become stiff. Over the years, Anna's health got worse and worse. She could not move her body and she was hospitalized many times. Most of all, communication with other people got harder as she lost control of the muscles of her mouth. It took a long time to understand what she was trying to say. In addition, her body was off balance, making her head and back lean to the side. This meant that she couldn't sleep well due to pain, and that she sometimes fell out of her bed. Paul was there to help his mother. However, every time he had to leave the hospital, he was worried about her falling off the bed and hurting herself. Whenever he left the hospital, Paul wanted to ask for extra care for the discomfort and danger this symptom might bring. However, every time Anna was newly hospitalized, different staff members took care of her, and they did not know about her unusual posture and its problems. Paul was tired of having to explain the situation to each staff member every time. Instead, he posted a note explaining that Anna's bent posture can be potentially dangerous. It also explained how to set up pillows to prevent her from falling off the bed. But people did not seem to notice it. He felt there was no one but him who could really take care of his mother. Frustrated, he went to get some fresh air. As he walked towards the elevator, he noticed a sign that said "DANGER" with an image of a person slipping on water. The sign warned people of the slippery floor with both a word and an image. All of a sudden, it occurred to Paul that comics could help. He was a comic writer after all! Using both words and pictures would surely help explain Anna's unusual posture and how to help her. Right away, he drew a comic consisting of a picture and a message on a piece of paper. He posted the note up on the wall above Anna's bed and then went home to get some sleep. The next morning when he got back to the hospital, he noticed that Anna's head had been supported with pillows just like the picture in the note. It seemed that the nurse had seen the picture and helped Anna. Anna slept comfortably and she was, most importantly of all, safe. This was the first comic Paul drew at the hospital, and he was surprised to see how well it worked. Realizing the potential of comics, Paul decided to ask Anna if there was anything she wanted to say to people. He sat down with her and asked her what comics he should draw. He patiently listened to her until he made sure he understood what she wanted. Finally, she asked Paul to draw a comic titled "Anna's Goal." In the comic, she wanted to look healthy, walking with her walker. She did not want herself to be seen as just another sick old lady in a hospital bed. Looking at this picture, the people around her began to think of her not just as a patient but as an individual who tries hard to achieve her goal. It led people around her, including hospital staff members, other patients, and visitors, to give words of encouragement and support whenever they saw her. Paul and Anna still face challenges. However, comics have been a great help in overcoming them. Comics can be powerful communication tools that take complex ideas and communicate them in a simple and efficient way. There is an old saying, "A picture is worth a thousand words." Paul's story shows that words and pictures work well together to tell stories, to communicate with others, to bring out kindness, and to create personal connections.

Paul's story shows that words and pictures work well together to tell stories, to communicate with others, to bring out kindness, and to create personal connections.

det.analysis:
❌ ① 그림을 그리려면 천 번의 연습이 필요하다는 뜻이 아님
✅ ② 한 장의 그림이 긴 설명보다 훨씬 많은 것을 효과적으로 전달한다는 뜻 ← 정답
❌ ③ 말이 그림보다 항상 더 정확하다는 뜻이 아님
❌ ④ 천 개의 단어를 알아야 그림을 이해한다는 뜻이 아님
det.tip: 그림 한 장 = 천 마디 말의 가치

questions.passage: He patiently listened to her until he made sure he understood what she wanted. Finally, she asked Paul to draw a comic titled "Anna's Goal." In the comic, <u>she</u> wanted to look healthy, walking with her walker. She did not want herself to be seen as just another sick old lady in a hospital bed. Looking at this picture, the people around her began to think of her not just as a patient but as an individual who tries hard to achieve her goal.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 she가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: she = Anna: 'Anna's Goal'이라는 만화 속에서 건강한 모습을 원한 사람은 Anna
det.analysis:
❌ ① 간호사: 문맥상 지칭 대상이 아님
❌ ② 병문안 온 방문객: 지칭 대상이 아님
❌ ③ Paul의 여동생: 본문에 없음
✅ ④ Anna ← 정답: 자신의 만화 'Anna's Goal'에서 건강한 모습을 원한 사람
det.tip: she = Anna (만화의 주인공)
